title: EEG-X: Toward Device-Agnostic and Noise-Robust Foundation Models for EEG
claim: A masked autoencoder reconstructs artifact-cleaned targets and compares them to outputs in a structured feature space, not raw signal space.
layout: Top-to-bottom, left-to-right flow; main pipeline above, zoomed 4-step inset below
description: A wide architecture diagram. At top left, raw multichannel EEG traces (AF3, AF4, F3, O1, O2) feed a dashed EEG tokenizer box. The box holds a purple location-based channel embedding and a blue signal embedding, which are summed into a column of blue tokens. The tokens are masked, passed through a transformer encoder, then a lightweight decoder, and come out as green reconstructed tokens. Below this, the raw EEG goes through a teal artifact-removal block to give cleaned EEG. Cleaned and reconstructed signals each pass through an orange DiCT block, and the two outputs meet at a yellow MSE-in-feature-space box with paired bar charts and the loss L_DiCT. Orange dashed arrows lead down to a large bottom inset that breaks DiCT into four numbered steps: input signal, dilated kernels, kernels competing at each time step, and win counts. The inset shows kernel icons, colored traces and count boxes, with formulas under steps 3 and 4.
caption: Architecture of EEG-X. EEG-X is built upon a masked autoencoding (MAE) framework and consists of three main components: (1) a signal embedding module augmented with location-based channel embeddings for handling heterogeneous EEG devices and channel layouts, (2) an artifact removal module that produces artifact-cleaned reconstruction targets from raw EEG signals, and (3) Dictionary-based Convolution Transformation (DiCT) objective for structured reconstruction learning.
abstract: Foundation models for EEG analysis are still in their infancy, limited by two key challenges: (1) variability across datasets caused by differences in recording devices and electrode configurations, and (2) the low signal-to-noise ratio (SNR) of EEG, where neural activity is often buried under artifacts and non-brain sources. To address these challenges, we present EEG-X, a device-agnostic and noise-robust foundation model for EEG representation learning. EEG-X introduces a location-based channel embedding that enables robust transfer across heterogeneous EEG devices and electrode layouts. To improve robustness against noise, EEG-X employs a novel noise-aware masking-reconstruction strategy that reconstructs artifact-cleaned signals rather than raw noisy EEG and introduces a novel Dictionary-based Convolutional Transformation (DiCT) that improves reconstruction-based pretraining by comparing signals in a structured feature space instead of directly in the raw signal space. Experiments across datasets collected from diverse EEG devices show that EEG-X consistently outperforms state-of-the-art methods across multiple downstream tasks and demonstrates strong cross-domain generalization when pretraining and downstream datasets differ in electrode layouts and recording configurations paving the way towards foundation models. The models and code are available at https://github.com/Emotiv/EEG-X.
